name: Stretches on exactly k venues
brief:
An order router logs the venue of each child order in turn. Compliance asks how many stretches of consecutive orders, of any length, touched exactly `k` different venues. Stretches at different places count separately, even when they hold the same venues.

Write `count_exact_venue_runs(venues, k)`, which returns that count.

Example. For `venues = ['L', 'C', 'L', 'T']` and `k = 2`, the stretches are `L C`, `C L`, `L T`, and `L C L`. So the answer is 4.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 100{,}000$ orders, each venue a string; $1 \le k \le n + 1$.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Growing a set from every start is too slow. Answers can pass $10^{9}$.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Exactly `k` is at most `k` minus at most `k - 1`. Counting stretches with at most `m` venues is one sliding window: each right edge adds the number of good stretches that end there.

examples.note: Three pairs and one triple touch two venues; `C L T` touches three.
Every one of the 6 stretches touches only `L`.

how: Submit runs 14 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. The obvious method grows a set of venues from every start, which is quadratic and runs out of time on the large tests. The step to the target is to count stretches with at most `k` venues and with at most `k - 1` with one sliding window each, and subtract.
notes: A window of at most `m` venues ending at `right` means every shorter stretch ending there qualifies too, so `right - left + 1` are added.
One window cannot count exactly `k` directly, since shrinking past the first good start loses stretches; the subtraction handles it.
Two passes, each with every order entering and leaving once, so the work is $O(n)$.

planted.slip: One window counts one stretch per right edge, missing the other good starts that end there.
Adding the whole window when it touches `k` venues counts short stretches inside it that touch fewer.
Shrinking by one order with `if`, not `while`, leaves windows that still touch too many venues.
